root_cause.text: The trusted-keys TPM2 loader `tpm2_load_cmd()` failed to release the temporary blob buffer returned indirectly by `tpm2_key_decode()` on error paths because its lifetime was tracked only by a conditional `if (blob != payload->blob) kfree(blob)` cleanup that did not reliably cover all exits.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that "`tpm2_load_cmd` allocates a temporary blob indirectly via `tpm2_key_decode` but it is not freed in the failure paths," and the patch fixes this by introducing `u8 *blob_ref __free(kfree) = NULL;`, assigning `blob_ref = blob` for the new-format decoded blob, and removing the old manual cleanup block `if (blob != payload->blob) kfree(blob);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an auto-free temporary buffer pointer in tpm2_load_cmd() to ensure allocated blob memory is cleaned up on function exit.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration was added at the start of tpm2_load_cmd(): `u8 *blob_ref __free(kfree) = NULL;`.
intent_record.how: This introduces an auto-cleanup pointer initialized to NULL, so if `blob_ref` is later assigned dynamically allocated memory in this function, it will be automatically freed on scope exit, reducing the risk of leaks on normal returns or error paths; as shown in this hunk alone, it does not otherwise change control flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Bind blob_ref to blob in the non-old-format path so shared cleanup code can correctly handle the new-format buffer.
intent_record.what: An else branch was added after the old-format payload handling in tpm2_load_cmd(), and inside it the variable blob_ref is assigned to blob with the comment "Bind for cleanup:".
intent_record.how: When the payload is not in the old format, blob_ref now explicitly points to the current blob so later cleanup logic can operate on the correct buffer reference, preventing the new-format path from lacking that cleanup binding.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop freeing `blob` in `tpm2_load_cmd()` cleanup to avoid an incorrect deallocation on the exit path.
intent_record.what: The cleanup code at the `out:` label in `tpm2_load_cmd()` was modified by removing a conditional block that checked `if (blob != payload->blob)` and called `kfree(blob)` when true, leaving only `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)` in that part of the exit path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change stops freeing the `blob` pointer during function cleanup, so any dynamically allocated buffer referenced by `blob` is no longer released at this exit point. This avoids deallocating that memory here, preventing a potentially incorrect free if ownership belongs elsewhere or the pointer may still be needed after this path.

grouping_result.intent: Stop freeing `blob` in `tpm2_load_cmd()` cleanup to avoid an incorrect deallocation on the exit path.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix tpm2_load_cmd() buffer ownership and cleanup so blob memory is managed correctly across old and new format paths without incorrect deallocation.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause in tpm2_load_cmd(): they fix ownership/lifetime tracking of the temporary blob buffer across format paths and ensure cleanup occurs correctly on error/exit paths, replacing the unreliable conditional free logic.

candidates.rationale: This conditional ownership check is the core flawed cleanup logic: freeing the temporary decode buffer depended on pointer inequality with payload->blob, which did not reliably represent allocation ownership across all paths, leading to missed frees on error exits.

This free was guarded by the incorrect ownership test above. The vulnerability is specifically about blob lifetime being tracked only through this conditional cleanup, so this deallocation statement is part of the faulty mechanism causing the leak on some error paths.

This assignment ties blob to payload->blob in the old-format path, contributing to the later pointer-comparison-based ownership model. Because cleanup relied on whether blob equaled payload->blob, this assignment is directly involved in the flawed lifetime tracking.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional embodies the flawed ownership/lifetime tracking for the temporary blob buffer. Cleanup on error depended on pointer inequality with payload->blob rather than explicit ownership of the buffer returned via decoding, so some error exits failed to release the temporary allocation.

This free is part of the vulnerable cleanup mechanism because it was executed only under the preceding incorrect pointer-comparison test. As a result, release of the temporary decode buffer was not reliably performed on all error paths.

This assignment contributes to the bug by making later cleanup logic infer buffer ownership from whether blob equals payload->blob. That pointer-identity model is the root of the unreliable error-path cleanup that caused the leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body of `tpm2_load_cmd()` is sufficient to judge the issue because it shows the allocation source (`tpm2_key_decode(payload, options, &blob)`), the fallback to `payload->blob`, the error returns, and the only cleanup site. The vulnerable construct is present: `tpm2_key_decode()` may allocate a temporary buffer and store it in `blob`, but `tpm2_load_cmd()` has multiple direct error returns before reaching the `out:` cleanup label. Specifically, after successful decode, the code does `if (!options->keyhandle) return -EINVAL;`, `if (payload->blob_len < 4) return -EINVAL;`, `if (private_len + 2 + 2 > (payload->blob_len)) return -E2BIG;`, and `if (private_len + 2 + public_len + 2 > payload->blob_len) return -E2BIG;`. If `blob` was allocated by `tpm2_key_decode()`, these early returns bypass the only free site: `if (blob != payload->blob) kfree(blob);` at `out:`. That matches the root cause: lifetime tracked only by conditional cleanup that does not cover all exits. Therefore the bug is present. The fix is not present because these early error paths do not jump to common cleanup and thus do not reliably free the temporary decoded blob.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full `tpm2_load_cmd()` body and the new helper `tpm2_key_decode()` that allocates the temporary buffer. The vulnerable construct is present in `tpm2_load_cmd()`: it calls `rc = tpm2_key_decode(payload, options, &blob);`, and on success `blob` may point to freshly allocated memory from `tpm2_key_decode()` (`blob = kmalloc(ctx.priv_len + ctx.pub_len + 4, GFP_KERNEL); ... *buf = blob;`). Cleanup is only done at the `out:` label via `if (blob != payload->blob) kfree(blob);`. However, there are multiple early returns after successful decode that bypass `out:` and therefore leak the allocated buffer: `if (!options->keyhandle) return -EINVAL;`, `if (payload->blob_len < 4) return -EINVAL;`, `if (private_len + 2 + 2 > (payload->blob_len)) return -E2BIG;`, `if (private_len + 2 + public_len + 2 > payload->blob_len) return -E2BIG;`, and `if (blob_len > payload->blob_len) return -E2BIG;`. Since the only free is conditional and located only in the `out:` path, these direct returns do not release the temporary `blob` allocated by `tpm2_key_decode()`. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not yet present because the function still relies on `if (blob != payload->blob) kfree(blob)` at the end instead of ensuring all error exits funnel through cleanup.
